seo.metaTitle: Palo Alto Car Accident Help | Personal Injury Attorney
seo.metaDescription: Injured in a Palo Alto car crash? Get a free case review from a personal injury attorney who works on contingency. No fee unless you recover.

hero.subtitle: After a collision on US-101, Middlefield Road, or Embarcadero Road, Palo Alto drivers deserve straightforward guidance, not more stress. We offer a free case review to help you understand what comes next.

about.title: Palo Alto Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Santa Clara County sees steady traffic through Palo Alto, and recent public records show 84 injury collisions and 106 people hurt in a single year, with crashes tending to cluster on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Corridors like US-101, Alma Street, and Embarcadero Road carry heavy volume, and even a routine commute can end in a jarring, life-altering collision. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the days right after matter: insurers move fast, evidence disappears, and recorded statements can be used against you later. We're a personal injury team that reviews the details of Palo Alto car accident claims, explains your options, and helps you avoid common missteps while you focus on recovering. There's no obligation and no upfront cost to get a case review.
commonInjuries: Cuts and bruising from broken glass or debris

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks dramatically — sometimes to six months — if a government entity, like the City of Palo Alto, was involved. We can flag this early so you don't lose your claim on a technicality.

items.title: Comparative Fault Cuts Both Ways
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your compensation is reduced by your share of blame. Insurers often try to shift fault onto you quickly, which is why it helps to have our team reviewing the facts before you say anything on record.

items.title: No Cap, No Guesswork on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases. Our team, working on contingency, has an incentive to value your claim fully, since we're only paid if you recover.

items.question: Do I have to give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: No, you're not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's often better not to until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened near a Palo Alto intersection maintained by the city?
items.answer: Claims involving city-maintained roads or intersections, such as those along Embarcadero Road or Middlefield Road, may fall under government claim rules with a much shorter filing deadline — sometimes as little as six months. It's important to have this evaluated quickly so you don't miss the window. We can review this promptly.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. Our initial case review is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. You're never obligated to move forward after speaking with us.
